OU-to-unit mapping drafted: which OU delegations become administrative units, and which become Azure RBAC scopes for servers

Name: Non-person identities inventoried (Non-Person Identity plan, Gate 0)

Name: Gate 0 — The tree read
Criteria (gates): Inventory in Git, site-linked GPOs included; every OU and every GPO half tagged with its track; a decision for every group; the OU-to-unit mapping drafted; nothing changed in the forest

Name: Program G0 — Ready to Plan: the read-only assessment committed
If late (decisions): The program plans Phase 1 without knowing what the OU tree encodes

Name: AD attribute inventory: which attributes are populated, by whom and how fully; which extension attributes are free to carry codes
Enterprise person key, and how source keys map to it (Identity Lifecycle plan, D-I1)

Name: AD-to-Entra mapping for every attribute that drives access, per object type: users, devices, Arc servers, service principals; the store for each from the store table
Attribute authority map signed (Identity Lifecycle plan, I1.2)

Name: Attribute schema: the store and the single writer for every attribute that drives access, in all four tracks
Options (decisions): Native properties first, then extension attributes 1–15 for what rules read, directory extensions for more slots, custom security attributes for sensitive values rules don't need, device properties, Azure tags and certificateUserIds (the store table); or a broader use of directory extensions from the start
If late (decisions): No slot can be assigned, and every group rule, persona and targeting convention waits

Name: The coded slot register: which extension attribute carries which code, on users and on devices
Owner or approver: Data architect, with HR for the code lists
Options (decisions): The program attribute map (organization, worker type and position category in extensionAttribute10 to 12; region, cost center, division, account type, clearance and DoNotSync in their slots; device tier, role and environment on the device object); or an agency map that keeps the same rule: codes, never names, one writer per slot
If late (decisions): Rules and filters are written against slots that may move, and every one is rewritten later

Name: Slot register published: one writer per slot, the code list owner, what reads it; the help desk, self-service and Exchange write paths listed for removal
Device, server and non-person attribute authorities named: the procurement record through the Autopilot group tag, the asset record through Arc onboarding tags, the owning system's record
Owner or approver: Data architect, with the endpoint lead

Name: Gate 1 — Schema and slots signed
Criteria (gates): Every attribute that drives access has one store, one writer and one owner, in all four tracks; the slot register published; the person key carried in employeeId in both directories; codes, never display names, in anything a rule reads

Name: Attribute taxonomy finalized (program P1.1)
If late (decisions): The program's taxonomy is finalized without the cross-track slot register

Name: HR data baselined; employeeId populated; orphan candidates owned (Identity Lifecycle plan, I1.5)
If late (decisions): The coverage baseline measures data the HR plan hasn't yet corrected

Name: Coverage baseline across the tracks: uncorrelated accounts, empty coded slots, counts per organization code against an HR export, duplicate keys; device and server attribute coverage
Correlation threshold before any rule grants access
Owner or approver: Authorizing official, through the agency's risk governance
Options (decisions): 99% of the pilot cohort correlated (a proposed starting point); a risk-tiered threshold, stricter for privileged and leaver-sensitive populations; 100% with a dated exception list
If late (decisions): No group can be piloted, because nobody has said how true the attributes must be

Name: Other write paths removed: help desk and self-service edits to the access slots, Exchange custom-attribute cmdlets, write rights on the target OUs
Entra ID sign-in, audit and provisioning logs routed outside Entra ID before the pilot's first change
Gate 2 — Attributes proven for the pilot
Criteria (gates): Correlation threshold met on the pilot cohort; every enabled account correlated or on a dated exception list; no duplicate keys; every other write path to the access slots removed in AD and Entra ID; logs leaving Entra ID

Name: Sync mapping for the slot register: carriers in the provisioning apps' target lists, date mappings, the transitional account-type rule, the DoNotSync filter; soft and hard match blocked
Sync and DNS Private Resolver designs (program P1.7)
If late (decisions): The sync design is approved without the attribute flow for the coded slots

Name: HR feed live for the foundation scope, shadow differences explained (Identity Lifecycle plan, Gate 3)
If late (decisions): The coded slots have no live writer, so the group library can't be shadowed on real data

Name: Gate 3 — Attributes flowing
Criteria (gates): Object counts within ±1%; no sync errors; every slot in the register arrives in Entra ID with the value HR sent; shadow-mode differences explained; both match types blocked outside a planned window

Name: Dynamic user group library: node and functional rules on codes; every access rule guarded by accountEnabled and userType and excluding agents' accounts; nesting flattened; no memberOf
Rules checked before they exist in production: guards, codes not names, paused processing; each rule tested against named users
Restricted management, unit by unit, before each unit exists
Options (decisions): No (the default): the unit scopes writes and stays in governance automation; yes, for a small set of sensitive accounts, accepting that they leave PIM, entitlement management, Lifecycle Workflows and access reviews
If late (decisions): A unit is created without the decision, and restriction can't be changed afterward

Name: Unit registry: tenant readers, department and division units whose rules mirror the group rules; scoped roles to PIM-eligible role-assignable groups; each unit created before the groups it holds
Gate 4 — Group library and units designed
Criteria (gates): Every governed group on one of the two patterns, on codes, with guards; every unit rule mirroring its group rule; restriction decided for every unit; every role assignment in the matrix

Name: Dynamic group design tested; enterprise groups and administrative units built (program P1.2)
If late (decisions): The program builds groups and units from a design that hasn't been checked

Name: Pilot attributes, groups and units going live (program P2.1, its start)
If late (decisions): There's no live pilot data to shadow the rules against

Name: Shadow comparison on the pilot: each dynamic group against the group it replaces, every add and remove explained; membership-delta alerts on
Pilot Conditional Access and Intune policies assigned (program P2.2, its start)
If late (decisions): Policies are assigned to groups whose membership hasn't been reconciled

Name: Conditional Access personas from coded attributes (worker type for internals and externals); every grant paired with a block; empty-slot users reported; emergency access excluded
The persona set the Conditional Access library targets
Options (decisions): The program's personas, built from the worker type and account type codes; personas plus division-specific overlays; fewer personas with more exclusions (not recommended)
If late (decisions): The Conditional Access design runs in report-only without the groups it will enforce on

Name: Conditional Access design running in report-only (program P1.5)
If late (decisions): Report-only runs against personas that may change

Name: Device targeting conventions: device slots written at registration by the provisioning service; dynamic device groups only where a rule reads tier or role; filters otherwise; no dynamic device group as an exclusion
Owner or approver: Endpoint lead, with the data architect

Name: Intune policy library built unassigned, with groups, filters and scope tags (Endpoint plan, E1.2, its start)
If late (decisions): The policy library is built on targeting the foundation may change

Name: Server targeting conventions: the Arc tag taxonomy drawn from the asset record and aligned with the device slots; resource groups as the delegation scope
Owner or approver: Server infrastructure, with the data architect

Name: Tag taxonomy fixed from the asset record (Endpoint plan, E4.2)
If late (decisions): Arc servers are tagged with a taxonomy the device and user sides don't share

Name: Non-person conventions: owners and sponsors recorded by the enterprise person key; custom security attributes for service principals (system, environment, tier) defined
Owner or approver: Identity engineering, with the identity governance officer

Name: AI accountability: sponsors mastered in HR (Non-Person Identity plan, N1.2, its start)
If late (decisions): Sponsors are recorded by name rather than by key, and a sponsor's move or departure can't be matched

Name: Gate 5 — Targeting conventions set
Criteria (gates): Personas from authoritative codes, grant and block in pairs, empty slots reported; device and server conventions published and handed to the Endpoint plan; non-person owners and sponsors keyed to the person key

Name: Binding coverage measured: certificateUserIds or altSecurityIdentities present and correct for every pilot card holder; the card management system named as the binding writer
Owner or approver: Identity engineering, with the PIV program office

Name: Required affinity binding for PIV and CAC
Options (decisions): High affinity in production (the program's position), with a custom rule per issuer during the pilot; low affinity until coverage is complete, with a dated end; mixed by issuer
If late (decisions): PIV sign-in goes to the pilot at the tenant default, which is low affinity

Name: High affinity piloted on the pilot cohort before the tenant setting changes; multifactor binding rule by issuer or policy OID
Certificate-based authentication for PIV and CAC holders (program P2.8)
If late (decisions): PIV sign-in reaches the pilot with bindings nobody has measured

Name: Who writes the binding after AD
Options (decisions): The card management system writes certificateUserIds through Microsoft Graph at issuance (design guidance, an open pilot); Entra Connect keeps syncing from altSecurityIdentities while any AD remains; manual entry by a Privileged Authentication Administrator (not at scale)
If late (decisions): User issuance can't move off AD CS, because nothing writes the binding without AD

Name: User and device issuance off AD CS; smart-card logon GPO retired (program P4.5)
If late (decisions): Issuance moves off AD CS with no writer for the binding

Name: Gate 6 — PIV binding proven on the pilot
Criteria (gates): Every pilot card holder bound; high affinity piloted with no lockouts; phishing-resistant strength for CBA users; the leaver removes the binding as well as revoking the card

Name: Joiner and mover automation (Identity Lifecycle plan, I4.3)
If late (decisions): There's no mover workflow to prove the foundation against

Name: Mover proof on the pilot: one personnel action moves a test user's organization code; groups, unit, persona and access packages change with no ticket; the device stays put; a drift scan comes back clean
Gate 7 — Mover proven across the tracks
Criteria (gates): The test mover's access changed only through the attributes, within the measured latency; nothing assigned by hand; the device's groups unchanged; the sponsor of any non-person identity the user sponsors notified; the change traced from the personnel action to the drift report

Name: Program G2 — Pilot Clean
If late (decisions): The pilot is called clean without a mover having been proved

Name: Drift severity and response times
Options (decisions): The program's classes (missing identity, stale access, orphan, attribute drift, unauthorized write, credential drift, schema drift) with high severity closed in days and the rest on a dated plan; a stricter clock for unauthorized writes to the access slots

Phase: Phase 9 — Drift, limits and steady state
Name: Limits register: dynamic group and rule limits, the 100-workflow Lifecycle Workflows budget, administrative unit limits, dynamic units' cloud availability; reviewed with every design change

Phase: Phase 9 — Drift, limits and steady state

Name: Gate 9 — Attributes kept true
Criteria (gates): Valid attributes for every HR-listed worker; every group on one of the two patterns; every unit rule mirroring its group with processing on; every policy targeting only governed groups; zero open high-severity drift findings; logs outside Entra ID; the six lifecycle metrics on the ConMon cadence
